marble.name: Parts of a circle
marble.subject: Mathematics
marble.description: Illustrate and name parts of circles, including radius, diameter, and circumference; know that the diameter is twice the radius
marble.prompt: If you give you a round plate and a ruler, can they measure the diameter — and explain how the radius compares to the diameter?

cluster.summary: Your child is exploring shapes and space — recognising circles, triangles, and squares, building with 3D shapes like cubes and spheres, and describing where things are using words like above, below, and beside.

misconceptions: Swaps radius and diameter, or substitutes a diameter where a radius is needed — the 'half/twice' error (NCTM).
Treats any line across the circle as a diameter, or draws a radius/diameter that does not reach or pass through the centre.
Applies the conversion in the wrong direction (doubles when it should halve), or thinks the radius equals the diameter.
representations: A labelled circle: centre, radius, diameter, circumference
Radius vs diameter vs an off-centre chord, contrasted
A radius/diameter table across several circle sizes
String wrapped round a circle to show the circumference as a length
authoredAnswer: The diameter is 9 cm, because the diameter is twice the radius (2 × 4.5). The centre-to-edge line is the radius and the edge-to-edge line through the centre is the diameter; a radius goes from the centre to the edge and a diameter passes through the centre, so the third line is neither (it is a chord) because it does not pass through the centre.
probe: Draw several straight lines from edge to edge across a circle, some through the marked centre and some not, and ask the pupil to PREDICT which line is longest before measuring — and to say why. wrongAnswers.wrong: 2.25 cm (halved the radius instead of doubling it)
wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Gives the diameter as 2.25 cm, or labels the centre-to-edge line as the diameter
wrongAnswers.fix: Draw and measure circles and tabulate radius against diameter to see the diameter is always double the radius; practise both conversion directions

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Picks the off-centre chord as the diameter, or draws a 'radius' that does not reach the centre
wrongAnswers.fix: Fold a paper circle to find the centre; only a line through the centre is a diameter (and it is the longest line across), and a radius must start at the centre

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Labels a straight line as the circumference
wrongAnswers.fix: Run a finger all the way round the edge — the circumference is the distance around, not a straight line across
